items.title: PM Anwar condemns Kedah MB Sanusi’s divisive comments, calls for unity
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has strongly condemned Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor over remarks suggesting that different ethnic groups in Malaysia could fall back on ancestral homelands outside the country. According to FMT, the Pakatan Harapan chairman said no leader should make statements that could offend other races, stressing that the Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities are loyal citizens who respect the Federal Constitution. "The Malaysian Chinese and Malaysian Indian communities respect the constitution and are loyal citizens.

items.title: Malaysia women-only trains gain global attention after French documentary feature
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's public rail network has captured international attention after being featured in the French travel documentary series Des trains pas comme les autres (Amazing Train Journeys). "In the Kuala Lumpur metro in Malaysia, certain carriages are reserved exclusively for women. Another user, @damien_mikeng, said the initiative reflected Malaysia's cultural values.

items.title: ‘There is no need to come to Negeri Sembilan’: Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, July 25 — Deputy Prime Minister and Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reminded Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor to steer clear of racial and religious sentiments during the Negeri Sembilan state election campaign. Astro Awani reported Zahid, Speaking to reporters after launching the “Madani Agriculture Commodity Programme” in Kuala Pilah today, said that if Sanusi truly wished to promote national unity, he should avoid touching on issues related to ethnicity, religion, culture or other racial backgrounds, as such remarks could stir unease among various communities. Zahid noted that Sanusi, who is also PAS’s election director for the state polls, may be accustomed to addressing Kedah’s electorate, but his style of speech may not sit well with the more diverse voters of Negeri Sembilan, where his words could be misinterpreted and cause unnecessary tension.

items.title: 'No need to come to Negri': Zahid tells Sanusi to focus on Kedah, avoid divisive rhetoric
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has cautioned Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor not to stir up racial and religious sensitivities in Negri Sembilan ahead of its state election. Zahid said the Kedah menteri besar should stay in Kedah for the remainder of the campaign period and focus on governing his state instead of campaigning in Negri Sembilan. Let us manage Negri Sembilan in our own way."

items.title: Rights body Suhakam voices concern over court ruling denying citizenship to children born out of wedlock
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — The Human Rights Commission of Malaysia (Suhakam) has expressed deep concern over a recent Court of Appeal decision that denies Malaysian citizenship to children born out of wedlock to Malaysian fathers and non-Malaysian mothers. While affirming full respect for judicial independence and acknowledging the court’s role in interpreting the Federal Constitution as it stands, Suhakam said the ruling exposes critical gaps in the country’s citizenship framework that could leave vulnerable children at risk of statelessness. “Every child has the right to acquire a nationality,” Suhakam said in a statement today, citing Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), to which Malaysia has been a signatory since 1995.

items.title: Anwar rejects Sanusi's 'Tanah Melayu' remarks, says Malaysia must embrace all citizens
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has rejected Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor's remarks on Tanah Melayu, saying Malaysia's strength lies in embracing all citizens. Anwar said Malaysia, independent for nearly 70 years, should not have leaders making statements that could insult or exclude other communities. He said while Malays were historically associated with Tanah Melayu, Malaysia's citizens came from diverse ancestral backgrounds and all who accepted the Constitution and contributed to the country must be regarded as part of the nation.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia given two years to tighten laws on forced labour imports under US trade deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Malaysia will have two years to introduce measures prohibiting imports of goods produced using forced labour under its trade agreement with the US, Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said today. He said the Human Resources Ministry had been informed of the changes required, including measures aimed at preventing Malaysian exports from incorporating imported materials or components produced through forced labour in third countries. Johari also addressed the US’ decision to impose a 10 per cent tariff on Malaysian imports following its investigation into countries that did not impose and effectively enforce restrictions on imports of goods produced using forced labour.

items.title: Loke urges NS election rivals to campaign positively, avoid arrogance
items.summary: JELEBU: All parties contesting the Negri Sembilan election should campaign positively and avoid arrogant statements DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the ultimate decision on the fate of any candidate or party rested entirely with the voters. We should campaign positively. "The local people know better than Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid.

items.title: China evacuates 20,000 people as Typhoon Noul nears
items.summary: BEIJING: Authorities have evacuated more than 20,000 people and suspended railway services in southern China as Typhoon Noul approaches, threatening torrential rain and gale-force winds, according to state media. The typhoon is forecast to make landfall along the coastal area stretching from Hong Kong to Guangdong province between Saturday evening and Sunday morning, China's National Meteorological Center said. Guangdong will suspend some train services on Saturday morning, with all rail services in the province to be halted on Sunday, CCTV said.

items.title: Anwar says decision on potential Formula One return to Malaysia will be announced tomorrow
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said developments regarding the possibility of Malaysia returning as a host for a Formula One (F1) race this year will be announced tomorrow. “The F1 matter will be announced on Sunday,” he said briefly when met by reporters after officially opening Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Agama Sheikh Tahir Jalaluddin and launching the Nuqaba programme here today. Yesterday, Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said the ministry was actively discussing and assessing the possibility of Malaysia hosting the race to replace the Bahrain Grand Prix, which is scheduled to take place in October.

items.title: Govt absorbs higher oil costs to keep RON95 at RM1.99, says Anwar
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is maintaining the RON95 petrol price at RM1.99 despite rising global oil prices by spending up to RM50 billion a year on fuel subsidies, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the government continued to shield consumers from higher fuel costs by absorbing billions of ringgit in subsidies, even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East pushed up crude oil prices and import costs. Anwar said Putrajaya was expected to spend between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually on fuel subsidies to keep pump prices low.

items.title: Man arrested over seditious, insulting Facebook post against Islam
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested a man for allegedly uploading a Facebook post containing seditious and insulting remarks against Islam. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said a report was lodged at 12.38am yesterday after a member of the public spotted the viral post on social media. "Checks showed that the owner of a Facebook account under the name 'Fadzil Zahari' shared several screenshots believed to have been uploaded by account owner 'Parthiban Ragu', which contained statements insulting Islam as well as offensive and obscene expressions directed at Allah SWT and Prophet Muhammad SAW.

items.title: Khaled: Expulsion of Israelis in line with Malaysia's longstanding policy
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Malaysia's decision to expel Israeli citizens aligns with its longstanding policy of not recognising Israel. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said Malaysia remained firm in its stance, and that enforcement action taken was in line with this policy. He said Malaysia's firm implementation of the policy had not affected funding under the IMET programme.

items.title: Malaysia one step closer to achieving high-income nation, says Ramanan
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Malaysia is one step closer to achieving high-income status after recording its highest Gross National Income (GNI) and economic output, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said. Speaking at the National Training Week (NTW) 2026 closing ceremony officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim here today, Ramanan said the latest World Bank data for 2025 showed Malaysia had made significant progress. He said Malaysia's GNI per capita, based on the World Bank's Atlas method, had reached US$12,380 — the highest since independence — while the country's economy expanded to a record GDP of US$472 billion.

items.title: Houthis claim strike on Saudi Arabia as conflict deepens
items.summary: SANAA: Iran-backed Houthi rebels claimed a missile strike on Saudi Arabia on Saturday, hours after vowing to retaliate against the kingdom for attacks as the Middle East war expanded. Saudi Arabia did not immediately comment on the claim. The Houthis claimed attacks on two Saudi ships earlier this week, with Saudi Arabia confirming one of the attacks in the Red Sea.

items.title: Bentong crash: Car went out of control on hilly, winding stretch
items.summary: BENTONG: The accident which claimed the lives of six friends on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Highway near Kampung Jambu Rias here early today occurred after their car went out of control on a hilly, winding stretch. The car then collided with an oncoming lorry, leaving the six occupants dead and the lorry driver seriously injured. Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the car was travelling from Kuantan towards Kuala Lumpur when it went out of control while negotiating a bend on the hilly stretch.

items.title: Take a hard look at yourselves before lecturing Malaysians on unity, Kasthuri tells Perikatan, PAS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Perikatan Nasional and PAS should “walk the talk” on national unity before lecturing Malaysians about it, DAP’s Kasthuri Patto said today, as she criticised the use of racial rhetoric during the Negeri Sembilan election campaign. “Malaysians must reject politicians who manipulate and exploit race and religion for their own political survival,” she said in a statement. Kasthuri was responding to remarks by PN election director and Kedah Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor, as well as Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, which she said had brought racial considerations into the campaign.

items.title: Anwar: Formula 1 announcement to be made on Sunday
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Malaysia's potential return to the Formula 1 calendar will be announced tomorrow, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said, amid uncertainty over races in the Middle East. Anwar, however, did not disclose details of the government's plans when asked about reports that Formula 1 could return to the Sepang International Circuit. A return would mark Malaysia's comeback to the Formula 1 calendar and could revive Sepang's position as an international motorsport destination.

items.title: Trump jokes about another term at rescheduled correspondents' dinner
items.summary: HAMILTON: US President Donald Trump joked about running for another term late on Friday as he donned a "Trump 2028" hat during the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Association (WHCA) annual dinner, Anadolu Ajansi (AA) reported. "I'm pleased to announce my intention to run for a fourth term as president of the United States," said Trump, before joking that he had "won three times" and was "getting very good at running for president". "But this place is really the largest group of Trump derangement syndrome people ever put together at one time," he said.

items.title: No one above the law, says Anwar, expects Cabinet nod to release Tabung Haji RCI report
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said no individual was above the law, as he stressed his government’s commitment to combating corruption and strengthening governance. Anwar also said he expects the Cabinet to agree to make the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Tabung Haji public when he tables the matter on Wednesday. “Maybank had also received global recognition for corporate governance and responsibility,” he said.

items.title: Johari: Voters to decide BN manifesto appeal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Voters in Negri Sembilan will ultimately decide whether Barisan Nasional's election manifesto is convincing enough to win their support, Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. "People in Negri Sembilan can evaluate it themselves because every party will come out with its own manifesto. When asked whether BN could expect stronger support from Chinese voters, Johari avoided speculation.

items.title: Johari: Malaysia gets two years to amend laws under US trade pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will have up to two years to amend its laws to address concerns over forced labour and excess industrial capacity once the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade (ART) with the United States is ratified. "They are giving us two years to amend the laws. However, he said the legal gap involved products made using forced labour overseas that entered Malaysia through global supply chains.

items.title: [UPDATED] Two men held after police chase involving Nissan Grand Livina
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Shamsudin Mamat said the incident began at about 11.57pm when the driver of a Nissan Grand Livina allegedly sped away from a police inspection at Persiaran Dagang, Sri Damansara. "When police attempted to make an arrest, the suspect acted aggressively by reversing the vehicle into a police patrol car before fleeing again. Shamsudin said police subsequently arrested the driver and his passenger, both men in their 50s, to assist with investigations.

items.title: Take a leaf out of MIC’s book, DAP MP tells MCA over response to Sanusi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — DAP’s Chong Zhemin has questioned MCA’s silence over racial remarks made by Perikatan Nasional election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor. According to Free Malaysia Today , the Kampar MP said MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran had already spoken out against the remarks despite Barisan Nasional’s electoral cooperation with PN in the Negeri Sembilan state election. “Yet MCA president Wee Ka Siong and the rest of the MCA leadership remain conspicuously silent.

items.title: [UPDATED] Suspect remanded over Klang cash van robbery bid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The suspect arrested over the attempted robbery of a cash-in-transit security van outside a bank in Bukit Tinggi, Klang, earlier this week has been remanded for six days to assist in investigations. "The suspect has been remanded for six days until July 29. On Monday, the suspect allegedly attempted to rob a security van carrying cash outside a bank in Bukit Tinggi, Klang.

items.title: Malaysia strongly condemns mass incursion into Al-Aqsa Mosque compound
items.summary: The Foreign Ministry said the deliberate and provocative act of storming Islam's third holiest site on Thursday was conducted under the protection of Israeli occupying forces and included an Israeli cabinet minister. It said the incident, accompanied by restrictions on Palestinian worshippers and unauthorised religious activities within the compound, constitutes a blatant violation of the historical and legal status quo governing the holy site. "Such actions also represent a grave breach of international law and relevant United Nations resolutions concerning the status of Occupied East Jerusalem.

items.title: Police propose merit system for students reporting bullying, extortion, and drugs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have proposed introducing a merit system for students who report bullying, extortion, or drug involvement in schools. Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said the proposal was among measures put forward to strengthen crime prevention following several violent attacks involving students. He said the system would help schools detect misconduct early and cultivate a culture of reporting.

items.title: Nail-free for nearly a century, Durah's heritage home stands the test of time
items.summary: Even more remarkably, the house, which stands on 12 pillars, was built without the use of a single iron nail. Instead, craftsmen of the past joined every timber component using the traditional pasak (wooden pegs) and tanggam (mortise-and-tenon) technique, a woodworking skill that has enabled the house to remain sturdy across generations. "This was originally my grandmother's house.

items.title: Prayer gathering ends in tragedy for crash victim [WATCH]
items.summary: TEMERLOH: One of the six victims of a pre-dawn crash in Bentong this morning had gone to attend a prayer ceremony with his family before heading out with friends, unaware it would be his final night. His sister, Moganah Vraputiran, 33, said Mugilan later went out with several friends after the ceremony in Sungai Kawang, including one who had recently returned from Singapore after a long absence. Mugilan was among six men aged between 15 and 25 killed in the crash.

items.title: Royal reassurance: Sultan of Terengganu in good health, continues treatment plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — The Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, is in good health and will continue his scheduled follow-up treatment abroad under the care of His Royal Highness’ medical team. The Office of the Sultan of Terengganu, in a statement shared by the Information Department today, said Sultan Mizan also expressed his deepest appreciation and gratitude to the people for their continued prayers for His Royal Highness’ health and well-being. “May Allah SWT continue to bless His Royal Highness the Sultan with good and lasting health, and ease all of his affairs,” the statement said.

items.title: Sultan Mizan in good health, to undergo follow-up treatment abroad
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sultan of Terengganu, Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin, is in good health and will undergo scheduled follow-up treatment abroad under the care of his medical team. The Office of the Sultan of Terengganu, in a statement released through the Information Department today, said Sultan Mizan expressed his appreciation to the people for their continued prayers for his well-being. "May Allah continue to bless His Royal Highness the Sultan with good and lasting health, and ease all of his affairs," the statement read.

items.title: Heavy fog cuts visibility in Sibu, disrupts air travel (VIDEO)
items.summary: SIBU, July 25 — Thick fog blanketed the riverine town today morning, significantly reducing visibility. Meanwhile, Deputy Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee said in a Facebook post that his flight from Kuching was unable to land in Sibu due to low cloud cover and fog at Sibu Airport. — The Borneo Post Dense fog shrouds the Rajang River in Sibu, leaving the waterway barely visible.

items.title: Police arrest student after baby’s body found at Kuala Langat hostel
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 25 — Police have arrested a female student in connection with the discovery of a baby’s body wrapped in cloth at a waste collection area of a hostel block at a higher learning institution (IPT) in Kuala Langat yesterday. Kuala Langat district police chief Supt Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said the teenage suspect was arrested following a report received from a local male informant regarding the discovery of the baby’s body at 12.20 pm yesterday. He urged anyone with information related to the incident to come forward at the nearest police station or contact the Kuala Langat district police headquarters (IPD) operations room at 03-3187 2222 to assist in the investigation.

items.title: Teenage student arrested after newborn's body found at university hostel
items.summary: KUALA LANGAT: A teenage student has been arrested after the body of a newborn baby wrapped in cloth was found in a university hostel rubbish disposal area here yesterday. District police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi said police received a report at 12.20pm from a man who discovered the infant's body at the hostel block's rubbish collection point. "Following investigations, police identified and arrested a teenage female student believed to be connected to the case to assist in investigations," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar urges Malaysians to consider RM50b fuel subsidy bill before listening to government critics
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, July 25 — The Madani government spends between RM40 billion and RM50 billion annually to keep RON95 petrol prices at RM1.99 per litre despite rising global oil prices, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. He said many neighbouring countries recorded significantly higher fuel prices, while the Madani government continued subsidising petrol and diesel to ease the burden on Malaysians. Besides fuel subsidies, Anwar said the government also allocates about RM15 billion to RM16 billion annually for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar urges youths to reject divisive narratives, engage with government
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has assured young Malaysians that the government is listening to their concerns while urging them to reject divisive ideologies. Anwar said the Madani government welcomed criticism and suggestions from young people, stressing that their feedback was essential to improving government programmes and ensuring no one was left behind. "Work together to build a stronger, more prosperous nation.

items.title: Anwar gives ministries one month to resolve foreign worker applications, prioritising restaurants
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has instructed the relevant ministries and departments to resolve foreign worker employment application issues according to priority, particularly for the restaurant sector, within one month. “So, insya-Allah, starting from Monday, I am giving the relevant ministries and departments a maximum period of one month to resolve foreign worker issues according to priority,” he said at the launch of the Indian Muslim Transformational Framework (IMTF) 2030 at the PICCA@Arena Butterworth Convention Centre here last night. Also present were Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow, Minister of Higher Education Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir, Minister of Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Steven Sim and Pertubuhan Gabungan Mukmin Nasional (Mukmin) president Datuk Shahul Dawood.

items.title: Fahmi: ICU to coordinate RM44.5m flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya, Damansara
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 25 — The RM44.5 million allocation announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for 30 flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya and Damansara will be coordinated through the Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU) of the Prime Minister’s Department. Earlier at the programme, the Prime Minister said the federal and Selangor state governments had agreed to approve 30 flood mitigation projects in Petaling Jaya and Damansara, involving a total allocation of RM44.5 million. Anwar said the flood mitigation projects were part of the government’s efforts to address areas identified as flood hotspots in Petaling Jaya and Damansara.

items.title: [UPDATED] Cabinet likely to approve Tabung Haji RCI report release, says Anwar
items.summary: PERMATANG PAUH: The Cabinet is expected to decide this Wednesday on whether to publicly release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji, says Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The prime minister said he had no objections to making the report public and would table the matter at the Cabinet meeting next week. When I bring it to the Cabinet on Wednesday, I believe the Cabinet will agree," he said at the closing ceremony of National Training Week 2026 today.

items.title: Two 14-year-old girls found dead at Ipoh flats, police investigations ongoing
items.summary: IPOH, July 25 — Two 14-year-old female students were found dead at Flat Sungai Pari here yesterday afternoon. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said police received a report on the incident in the afternoon and initial investigations found that the two victims had left the school before they were found unconscious and later pronounced dead at the scene. He urged anyone with information about the incident to contact the Ipoh District Police Operations Room at 05-2451500 or the nearest police station to assist with the investigation.

items.title: Crisis-hit Flavio Bolsonaro launches presidential candidacy in Brazil
items.summary: SAO PAULO: Battered by a string of political crises, Flavio Bolsonaro will formally launch his candidacy for Brazil's October presidential election on Saturday, seeking to follow in the footsteps of his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The Liberal Party (PL) will officially name Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, as its candidate at a convention in Sao Paulo, with Argentina's libertarian President Javier Milei as a guest of honour. Flavio is promising change: he wants to "free" Brazil from crime, inflation, high taxes and Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.

items.title: Six detained in ketum processing operation across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan
items.summary: The six were arrested during a three-day integrated operation across Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan, which ended on Thursday. General Operations Force (GOF) Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the operation, codenamed Op Bersepadu MITRA 1/26, began on July 21. He said the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) of Pahang, Terengganu and Kelantan.

items.title: Malaysia aims to produce first locally made human vaccine by 2028
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Malaysia is reprotedly aiming to produce its first locally manufactured human vaccine as early as 2028, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang reportedly said. The Sta r reported Chang as saying the vaccine would be a 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine, or PCV13, produced by Pharmaniaga Bhd through a technology transfer arrangement with a Chinese company. Chang reportedly said that producing vaccines locally would lessen Malaysia’s reliance on overseas supplies and improve its ability to respond to future public health crises.

items.title: MCMC probes Facebook post allegedly insulting Islam
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is investigating a complaint over Facebook content touching on race, religion and royalty (3R) that allegedly insulted Islam. In a statement today, MCMC said it would not compromise on any misuse of communication platforms that violates the law. MCMC said the dissemination of such content was viewed seriously as it could incite hatred, undermine social unity and threaten national harmony.

items.title: MINDEF: LIMA'27, DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028 gain global industry backing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition 2027 (LIMA'27), as well as the Defence Services Asia (DSA) and National Security (NATSEC) Asia 2028 exhibitions, have received early commitments from several leading global defence industry players to participate in the events. The Ministry of Defence (MINDEF), in a statement, said the early commitments reflected growing confidence among global defence and aerospace industry players in Malaysia's capability to host international-standard defence exhibitions. "The development further strengthens LIMA'27 and DSA & NATSEC Asia 2028 as leading international platforms for the defence, aerospace and security sectors, while creating opportunities for strategic cooperation and supporting the growth of the defence industry," it said.

items.title: Ramkarpal: Umno’s silence over PAS racial remarks may be ‘sign of things to come’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Umno’s silence over racial remarks by PAS leaders could set the tone for their new-found political cooperation in Negeri Sembilan, DAP’s Ramkarpal Singh said today. Ramkarpal said Sanusi’s remarks were insensitive to non-Malays and implied that Malaysian Indians and Chinese did not belong in the country because they could supposedly return to India or China. Ramkarpal further called on the authorities to immediately investigate Sanusi, saying failure to act risked similar remarks being repeated during the Negeri Sembilan election campaign.

items.title: Teen found dead after suspected fall from Komtar, police say no evidence of foul play
items.summary: Timur Laut police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report from a member of the public regarding the incident at 4.05pm. He said preliminary investigations identified the victim as an 18-year-old local male from the Macallum area. Abdul Rozak said preliminary investigations found no evidence of foul play.

items.title: Police bust gun-smuggling network operating for seven years, seize RM360,000 in weapons
items.summary: KANGAR, July 25 — Police have crippled a firearms smuggling syndicate after seizing weapons worth RM360,000 and arresting eight individuals, including a civil servant, in operations across Perlis, Perak, and Kedah this month. Perlis Police chief Datuk Muhammad Abdul Halim said the syndicate has been active since 2019. Muhammad said the crackdown began after the Perak contingent police headquarters (IPK) Criminal Investigation Department (CID) arrested a man in Sitiawan on July 1.

items.title: Six killed in crash on Jalan Karak Lama [WATCH]
items.summary: Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said the department's operations centre received an emergency call at 4.24am, prompting a team from the Karak Fire and Rescue Station to rush to the scene. He said the first fire engine arrived at 4.32am and found the crash involving a Toyota Camry and a one-tonne lorry. "Six male victims in the Toyota Camry were found trapped in the vehicle and were pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel," he said in a statement today.

items.title: ‘Old politics of fear and race must end’: Anwar looks to Gen Z for change
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said political leaders must be chosen from among those who are capable of embracing the strength to unite the country, not create division. “We should not inculcate fear among the Malays against the Chinese, among the Chinese against the Indians, among the Indians against the Dayak. “We bring change, reform.

items.title: BN committed to Unity Govt until term ends, whatever Negeri Sembilan result, says Zahid
items.summary: JELEBU, July 25 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has reaffirmed that leaders of the Unity Government remain committed to working together at the federal level until the end of the current term, regardless of the upcoming outcome of the Negeri Sembilan state election. He said his relationship with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remains good, describing their working relationship as cordial and professional. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Students who attacked father and son in Seri Kembangan fight undergo counselling, says Selangor Education Dept
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 25 — The Selangor Education Department (JPN) has carried out counselling and guidance interventions for students involved in a fight involving a student and his father at a secondary school in Seri Kembangan that went viral recently. “Selangor JPN views seriously the fight involving a group of students as reported by the media and circulated online recently. “The department is extending its full cooperation to the ongoing investigation.

items.title: BN unveils nine-pillar election manifesto to ‘revitalise’ Negeri Sembilan
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 25 — Barisan Nasional (BN) yesterday launched its manifesto, outlining nine key pillars for the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election. The manifesto, themed ‘ Hebatkan Semula Negeri Sembilan ’ (Revitalising Negeri Sembilan), was launched by Negeri Sembilan BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, who is also the BN deputy chairman. Also present were Negeri Sembilan UMNO Liaison Committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias, who is also its Negeri Sembilan Election director, MCA deputy president Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon, MIC vice-president Datuk M. Asojan and BN candidates contesting in the election, as well as Perikatan Nasional (PN) deputy chairman Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.

items.title: ‘Malaysia is proud’: Anwar congratulates Alif Rakib on becoming country’s first ONE Muay Thai world champion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national Muay Thai fighter Ahmad Nor Iman Aliff Rakib, known as Alif Rakib, after he became the first Malaysian to win a ONE Championship Muay Thai world title. Alif Rakib won the ONE Championship Interim Strawweight Muay Thai World Title after defeating Thailand’s Sam-A Gaiyanghadao. The victory earned Alif Rakib a US$50,000 (RM204,565) performance bonus and the championship belt.

items.title: Father gets 60 years’ jail for raping daughter who later gave birth to his child
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 25 — An Indonesian man was sentenced to 60 years in prison and 60 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here yesterday after pleading guilty to six counts of raping his biological daughter until the victim gave birth to a baby girl. Deputy Public Prosecutor Banusha Jegathesan requested a severe sentence considering that the accused was the biological father of the victim who was given the responsibility to take care of her child, but the accused acted otherwise. “The accused was also previously accused of molesting the victim’s child.

items.title: We have raised the ‘ceiling’; Now we must raise the ‘floor’
items.summary: JULY 25 — GDP estimates indicated that Malaysia’s economy grew by 5.8 per cent in Q2 2026, from 5.4 per cent in Q1 2026, exceeding market expectations yet again. For the first half of the year, growth stood at 5.6 per cent, compared with 4.5 per cent during the corresponding period last year. An against-the-odds growth story The story behind our growth is partly supported by manufacturing – which expanded by 7.5 per cent in Q2 2026, up from 5.9 per cent in Q1 2026 – driven by E&E and optical products.

items.title: From wedding thalis to temple decor, Penang goldsmith preserves generations of craftsmanship
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 25 — For fourth-generation goldsmith Raju Murugesan, every piece of jewellery he made was forged by hand, each intricate detail painstakingly carved, a skill that was handed down in his family for generations. Raju said he learnt the trade from his parents and has been making jewellery by hand ever since. Each piece of jewellery was handmade by Raju Murugesan at their shop in Queen Street.

items.title: Anwar says PJ, Subang development funds still available but not through MPs who oppose govt
items.summary: Responding to claims that constituency allocations had been withheld, Anwar insisted that the government had not cut funding for the people, but had stopped disbursing certain allocations through MPs who no longer supported the government. The people want projects or MPs want projects? The people want projects.

items.title: Marine police seize RM6.12m syabu shipment bound for Indonesia off Pulau Rimau
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 24 — The Region One Marine Police Force (PPM) in Penang has foiled an attempt to smuggle drugs worth about RM6.12 million to Indonesia during ‘Op Taring Gelora’ in the waters off Pulau Rimau last week (July 17). Bukit Aman Department of Internal Security and Public Order (KDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the operation was launched following intelligence from the Marine Intelligence Unit (URM) on the movements of a fibreglass boat carrying two Indonesian men suspected of smuggling drugs to Indonesia. Also present were Penang Police Chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng and Marine Police Force Commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Shamsol Kassim.
